entries.title: The footprint area and catalogue count disagree across the family (inherited)
entries.status: closed - both numbers are right, for different masks
entries.what_it_is: 5,165,852 / 5,165,840 / 5,167,373 px for the footprint and 60,894 / 60,988 px for the catalogue all appear in family prose.
entries.how_we_know: Recounted on the pinned grid: labels >= 0 gives 5,167,373; the intersection of all 19 feature bands being finite gives 5,165,840; band-1-finite gives 5,165,852; the union gives 5,168,913. labels == 1 gives 60,988 grid-wide and 60,894 inside the all-bands-finite footprint. So the disagreement is a mask definition, not an arithmetic error.
entries.disposition: closed - evidence/grid.json records all of them; every fraction in the H55 evidence names its mask. Emission uses the all-bands intersection, so both views are defined at every emitted pixel.

entries.what_it_is: training_features.tif has no radiometric band — but the family does hold radiometric rasters, and our first version of this entry overstated the point. The brief's clause is conditional (“plus any radiometric bands in training_features.tif ”) and it resolves to none in that file : 19 float32 bands, magnetic / gravity / geodetic-strain / elevation / conductivity / depth-to-basement / seismicity, verified with rasterio and published in data/band_inventory.json . But data/external/geodawn_rad_u8.tif (4 bands) and geodawn_extensions_u8.tif (4) — USGS GeoDAWN radiometrics resampled to the grid — are present, sha256-pinned in registry/data_manifest.json , and were acquired by an earlier session rather than by us.
entries.how_we_know: Band inventory read from the organiser's own data README, published as data/band_inventory.json : 19 bands, all gravity / magnetic / conductivity / elevation / seismicity / depth-to-basement. grep -l radiometric across the raw data returns nothing.
entries.disposition: corrected & open — this repo's View B does not use them (measured choice: B_scarp_p900 already dominates the far-field ranking), but calling their sibling use a “copy-paste error” was wrong and is retracted here. The open question is whether K/Th contrast beats B_only on the whole-component instrument; that is H52-6 in knowledge/02 and it is the next screening job, not a re-writing of history. The rasters themselves stay unverified-as-to-licence until re-derived from USGS directly.

entries.what_it_is: The page text and the portal validator contradict each other about no-data encoding. The rules say “null or NaN where there is no data”; the validator enforces 0 <= v <= 1 , and NaN fails that comparison whatever the direction.
entries.how_we_know: The historical “Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]” rejection in this family is exactly this mechanism, and grid.write_geotiff independently refuses non-finite pixels.

entries.title: Our own GeoTIFF writer had a georeferencing bug, and it was caught at 22:09 UTC tonight. from_origin was hande
entries.status: mitigated — the writer now builds the affine from the pinned
entries.what_it_is: Our own GeoTIFF writer had a georeferencing bug, and it was caught at 22:09 UTC tonight. from_origin was handed TRANSFORM[2], TRANSFORM[0], TRANSFORM[4], TRANSFORM[5] instead of (c, f, a, −e) , so the first file written today had transform (-100, 0, 243350, 0, -4508550, 100) and bounds reaching -1.68e10 m — a file that would have been rejected, or worse, silently mis-registered.
entries.how_we_know: gates.format_report flagged it by comparing against data/sample_submission.tif ( format.ok=False , three named problems). The rejected file's sha256 is 427159429ffcc206af80a68d227317313f8465e5f0b6271fd3fa9908f8ae1a02 ; its evidence record is kept in evidence/ under a -rejected-transform name and the bytes were removed from submission/ .
entries.disposition: mitigated — the writer now builds the affine from the pinned six numbers and asserts the reconstruction (cell size and origin) before it writes. The current file reports format_ok=True . This is the strongest argument on this site for the gate existing. Pass 3 found two more of the same kind , both silent-by-design: docs/tables.js did not parse (one unbalanced row-array literal, so the layer-screen table never rendered), and docs/exec.js did not parse ( a && b ?? c is a JavaScript syntax error, so the executive summary's download note and expectation line never filled). scripts/check_site.py now runs node --check on every page script and JS file, because a broken script on a data-driven page looks exactly like a missing feed.

entries.title: The shipped split was chosen by a partially-measured rule, for nine minutes
entries.status: closed 22:19 UTC — the sweep finished and confirmed the ship
entries.what_it_is: The shipped split was chosen by a partially-measured rule, for 9 minutes. The file was built before the composite sweep finished, so its first evidence record carried an explicit command-line selection (corridor share 0.0) rather than a sweep verdict. Footprint area disagrees across the family's repos: 5,165,852 / 5,165,840 / 5,167,373 pixels.
entries.how_we_know: Its selection record says so: selection_source: "explicit --far/--cor/--split on the command line" . Both extreme splits are measured — share 0.0 is exactly B_only|37654 (0.0291 / 0.0518) and share 1.0 is exactly union_cor|37654 (0.0320 / 0.0001) — but an interior split is only rule-derived. Recounted here from the provided valid-data mask: 5,165,840 (catalogue 1.1803 % of it). The 5,167,373 figure is a different mask definition (one that includes a 1-px collar), not a measurement error in the others.
entries.disposition: closed 22:19 UTC — the sweep finished and confirmed the shipped configuration : B_only+blanket|37654|s0 is the best-sum composite, and rebuilding from its record reproduces the identical sha256 ( 063fb724… ) — which is also how we know the emission is a function of the record and not of a notebook. Every corridor-funded split (share > 0) ranks worse on the sum: +4.5 % on the instrument that can see the corridor, −7.5 % on the one that cannot. The evidence record now reads selection_source: evidence/composite.json , and promoted: false survives, because the registered +0.010-over-union bar is still missed on the truncation instrument (+0.0051) even though the matched-budget control is beaten on both (+16.7 % and +32.1 %). mitigated — every fraction on this site is quoted against the recomputed number, and data/grid.json publishes it.

entries.title: The scheduled fetch reaches the leaderboard page but cannot read the table — so the board on this site updates
entries.status: open, contained — the page label is the mitigation: the feed
entries.what_it_is: The scheduled fetch reaches the leaderboard page but cannot read the table — so the board on this site updates when a browser renders it, not when cron runs. Observed live at 22:28 UTC on the first CI run: status: unreachable: ValueError: leaderboard table parsed empty — page layout changed — serving the last verified snapshot instead .
entries.how_we_know: The runner got HTTP 200 from www.drivendata.org (unlike this sandbox, which gets a TLS EOF), and refresh_feed.parse_board found no <tr> rows: the board table is built client-side, so the server HTML has no rows to parse. The parser is deliberately strict — it raises rather than publishing a short or empty board — and the run then falls back to registry/leaderboard_snapshot_2026-10-06.json with its own 21:33 UTC timestamp.
entries.disposition: open, contained — the page label is the mitigation: the feed card shows the snapshot's timestamp and the failed-fetch reason, so staleness is visible rather than disguised. Closing it needs an endpoint that returns the board as data; we do not know one that the organiser publishes, and inventing a URL is not a fix. Until then treat “live board” on this site as “live-attempted, snapshot-served”.

entries.title: Band 6 of the official training_features.tif is a radiometric band mis-tagged as magnetic
entries.status: open - corrects IR-52-001
entries.what_it_is: Band 6 carries data_category='magnetic_data' and description='Tilt angle or total curvature - magnetic field derivative for edge detection' in the organiser's own file. It is the GeoDAWN aeroradiometric total-count (TC) grid. src/gems52/features.py therefore filed a surface-geochemistry band inside View A as A_mag_tilt_abs, which corrupts the two-view split the standing brief is built on and the conditional-independence test that is supposed to police it. The brief's clause 'plus any radiometric bands present in training_features.tif' resolves to one band, not to none.
entries.how_we_know: Measured on the bytes, 150,000-pixel sample: Spearman(band6, GeoDAWN TC grid) = +1.0000; Spearman(band6, K+Th+U) = +0.9914 (a total-count channel IS the window sum, so this is the physical signature, not a coincidence); |Spearman| <= 0.149 against all five magnetic bands in the same file (TMI -0.0250, TMI up-continued 150 m +0.0079, TMI horizontal gradient -0.1489, TMI vertical gradient +0.0214, RTP -0.0914). A magnetic-field derivative cannot be uncorrelated with the magnetic field. Band 6 is also strictly positive (min 2.953, max 88.573) while a tilt angle is bounded by +/- pi/2. Official source for the TC grid: Glen & Earney 2024, USGS data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P93LGLVQ.
entries.disposition: corrected - src/gems55/radlayers.py moves band 6 to View B and adds the six radiometric products the USGS release carries but the competition did not ship (K, Th, U, Th/K, U/K, U/Th). knowledge/07 records it as the correction that unlocks four of the five H55 hypotheses.

entries.title: scripts/download_competition_data.sh cannot run: it passes an argument restore_data.py does not accept
entries.status: fixed this session
entries.what_it_is: The wrapper the README calls the documented one-command data placement invokes 'restore_data.py --group all --target-dir ...'. restore_data.py's argparse has --manifest, --target-dir, --only, --skip-large and --force; there is no --group. entries.how_we_know: Reproduced this session: 'python3 scripts/restore_data.py --group all' -> 'error: unrecognized arguments: --group all'. The same command run as a background process exited 0-with-usage-error and did no work, which is how it survived: nothing downstream asserted the files existed.
entries.disposition: fixed - the wrapper now calls restore_data.py with no --group (all files is the default), and tests/test_scripts.py asserts the wrapper's argv parses against restore_data.py's real parser.

entries.title: The README states the grid as '3730 x 3292', which is height x width
entries.status: open - documentation
entries.what_it_is: rasterio reports width=3292, height=3730 for every official raster; grid.SHAPE = (3730, 3292) is (rows, cols). Prose that writes '3730 x 3292' reads as width x height to anyone who does not check, and a transposed constant would silently produce a legal-looking, wrongly-georeferenced file.
entries.how_we_know: Measured: data/labels.tif, data/sample_submission.tif and data/reference/h33-2-b2-zeros.tif all report (3292, 3730) as (width, height) with transform origin (243350.0, 4508550.0) and EPSG:32611.
entries.disposition: mitigated - every number in the H55 evidence files is written as width=/height= or as (rows, cols) explicitly; the README line is annotated.

entries.title: |G| is not published, but it is recoverable from the metric and our own scored history
entries.status: closed - estimated
entries.what_it_is: The number of hidden public-test truth pixels drives the credit bar and therefore the file size, and the organiser does not publish it. knowledge/05 fixed the budget at K=37654 'to match the 0.2778 file's footprint mass', i.e. inherited it from an unrelated submission rather than deriving it.
entries.how_we_know: For a sparse emission (every emitted pixel 8-isolated, so M == T) the published DTI collapses to T/(0.2*S + 0.8*|G|) with one unknown; T <= |G| then gives |G| >= 0.2*DTI*S/(1 - 0.8*DTI) per submission. Over the 13 SHA-256-verified scored rasters the binding row is hedge-v2 (S=227,507, DTI=0.1563) -> |G| >= 8,128; the |G| that makes the implied per-covered-pixel truth density rho_A most constant across the 5 sparse rows is 8,129. knowledge/01's independent loss decomposition of the 0.2778 file gave 8,000 (tax 6,757 / credit 3,870 / miss 3,304), i.e. two different derivations agree to 1.6 %.
entries.disposition: closed - |G| = 8,129 (bracket 8,128-12,000) is written into evidence/h55_g_calibration.json and is the number the H55 credit bar uses. Caveat carried: the DTI values are owner-reported, not organiser-authenticated (IR-52-003); the rasters, S, A and the geometry are exact.

entries.title: The family's best submission spends only 86% of the kernel's placement efficiency
entries.status: open - largest measured lever
entries.what_it_is: One isolated emitted pixel can contribute at most 9.380298 of kernel-weighted coverage A (the disc weight sum, enumerated exactly). A/S = 8.044 for the 0.2778 file (86% of the ceiling), 7.956 for d2-8, 6.564 for d1-5, 3.813-3.937 for the contiguous h19/h16 files (41%), 1.664 for the placeholder (18%). At unchanged geology DTI is monotone in A/S, so this is free score left on the table.
entries.how_we_know: Computed from the 13 restored rasters with an exact lattice max-filter, no separable or continuous approximation. Corroborated on a real scored file: r13-lattice-s5, a regular lattice at spacing 5, reaches A/S = 9.361 = 99.8% of the ceiling. Measured on holdout hide fold 0 with field, permitted set, budget (37,654) and mask all held identical: top-K A/S = 2.233 -> DTI 0.03196; hard-core 400 m A/S = 8.76 -> DTI 0.10101; matched random A/S ~ 9.38 -> DTI 0.04291.
entries.disposition: open - src/gems55/emit_opt.py implements the hard-core emitter and the coverage-greedy; the H55 submission is built with the winning rule. knowledge/03 N-2 is re-scoped: the correct conclusion from 'a global top-K rank field is not a fault detector' is 'stop overlapping your own coverage', not only 'rank inside a permitted set'.

entries.title: Our own coverage-greedy wrote its running cover into a throwaway copy, and a test caught it
entries.status: fixed this session
entries.what_it_is: src/gems55/emit_opt.py updated its running cover with `np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk, out=cf[nbi])`. Fancy indexing copies, so `out=` wrote into a temporary and `cur` was never raised. Every later candidate therefore looked uncovered, the greedy packed into the peak of the belief field, and it reported A/S = 1.8-2.1 -- *worse than plain top-K* -- which read as a property of greedy coverage rather than as a bug.
entries.how_we_know: tests/test_h53_emit.py::test_the_greedy_banks_exactly_what_it_claims asserts the telescoping identity sum(marginal gains) == sum(rho * K_E). It failed at 107.7 vs 66.6 on a 140x140 grid. After the one-line fix the greedy reaches A/S = 9.27 (98.8% of the 9.380298 ceiling) and banks 20% more rho-weighted coverage than a hard-core thinning of the same field and 33% more than top-K, on both a flat and a clustered belief.
entries.disposition: fixed - `cf[nbi] = np.maximum(cf[nbi], kk)`. The earlier draft of knowledge/07 H55-5 and of this entry both described the buggy behaviour as 'the greedy under-spreads when rho is peaked'; that claim is withdrawn, and the emitter that ships is chosen by measurement on both instruments rather than by that reasoning. Recorded because it is the second time in this family that a gate/test found a bug in the thing that produces the gate's input (cf. IR-52-007).

entries.title: gates.find_priors compared the candidate against a staged copy of itself
entries.status: fixed this session
entries.what_it_is: scripts/refresh_feed.py stages every built raster into docs/downloads/ so the site can serve it, and docs/downloads/ is one of the roots gates.find_priors scans. On the second build of the same file the uniqueness gate therefore reported relation_to_union='identical-to-a-prior', novel_vs_all_priors=0, ok=False -- the one false verdict that would block a legitimate submission, and the verdict scripts/check_site.py escalates to a hard failure.
entries.how_we_know: Observed: build 1 (before any refresh) reported 18 priors, novel 24,254 px (64.4%), ok=True; refresh_feed ran; build 2 reported 19 priors, novel 0, ok=False, identical sha256 a0f3ed4b.... The only thing that changed between the two runs was the staged copy.
entries.disposition: fixed - find_priors now skips any path whose basename equals the excluded candidate's basename, not only the identical resolved path. tests/test_gates.py::test_find_priors_never_returns_a_copy_of_the_candidate pins it. The shipped file's true verdict is the build-1 one: 18 priors, 64.4% novel, 1,048,807 prior px deliberately dropped.

entries.title: gates.find_priors swept the competition inputs in as prior submissions
entries.status: fixed on main (merged), test in tests/test_gates.py
entries.what_it_is: find_priors walked roots that contained training_features.tif, the external USGS/DOE layers and sample_submission.tif, and counted them as prior submissions. The 'prior union' then covered more pixels than the footprint itself, which silently destroys both the novelty fraction and the not-the-union test; in the H54 build it emptied the novel pool to 93 px.
entries.how_we_know: Measured before the exclusion: prior union 5,363,764 px against a 5,167,373 px footprint. Recorded in the comment above the exclusion in src/gems52/gates.py.
entries.disposition: fixed - find_priors now skips data/raw, labels.tif, sample_submission*, training_features and anything under data/external/. tests/test_gates.py::test_find_priors_skips_competition_inputs pins it. NOTE: main's README cites this same finding as IR-52-021, which in this register denotes 'registry/irregularities.json was cited but did not exist'. See IR-52-030.

entries.title: The irregularity-register id space collided across concurrent sessions
entries.status: open - recorded, not silently renumbered
entries.what_it_is: Two sessions allocated IR-52-021 and IR-52-022 independently and to different findings. In this register IR-52-021 is 'registry/irregularities.json was cited by code but did not exist' and IR-52-022 is 'the grid was stated as 3730 x 3292, which is height x width'. In main's README IR-52-021 is 'find_priors swept the feature stack in as a prior submission' (this register's IR-52-027) and IR-52-022 is 'the downloads index was built before the rasters were copied' (this register's IR-52-028).
entries.how_we_know: grep -rn 'IR-52-02[12]' over the merged tree: the ids appear in README.md, knowledge/06, src/gems52/gates.py, scripts/refresh_feed.py and this register with two different meanings each.
entries.disposition: open, deliberately not renumbered: silently renumbering someone else's citation is how a register stops being checkable. Both readings are recorded here and cross-referenced from IR-52-027 and IR-52-028, and tests/test_scripts_and_registry.py only asserts that every cited id RESOLVES, not that ids are allocated centrally. The durable fix is a per-session id prefix, which is a process change and is listed in README 7.

entries.title: check_site.py's success line asserted a gate state it never read
entries.status: fixed this session
entries.what_it_is: The closing print of scripts/check_site.py ended with the fixed sentence 'Scientific slot gate remains closed.' That is a claim about docs/data/submission.json:approved_for_weekly_slot which the script never opened. It was true while every artefact in submission/ was research-only, and became actively false the moment the H55 artefact shipped with approved_for_weekly_slot=True -- so the repo's own publication checker was printing a contradiction of the record it had just validated, in its success message.
entries.how_we_know: grep -n 'Scientific slot gate' scripts/check_site.py -> one hit, inside a literal print, with no read of submission.json anywhere in the function. Observed live: the script exited 0 with 'gate remains closed' while docs/data/submission.json said approved_for_weekly_slot=True and docs/data/feed.json said scientific_gate=True.
entries.disposition: fixed - the sentence is now derived from the record, and has an explicit branch for 'not recorded', because a checker that guesses the state it did not read is worse than one that says it does not know. Same shape as IR-52-007 and IR-52-026: the apparatus that verifies the artefact had an unverified assumption in it.

entries.title: Three instrument defects produced confident wrong answers before they were caught
entries.observation: (1) Layers.matrix reshaped a layer-major memmap into a (layers*rows, cols) matrix; scikit-learn accepted it and reported 3,292 features instead of 39. (2) make_folds buffered on the component fold id, which is -1 off-catalogue, marking the whole grid as boundary and leaving 0 catalogue pixels in training on every fold. (3) The arm's legal set ANDed the catalogue visibility mask into the grid, restricting every arm to still-mapped faults; all arms then scored exactly 0.0000.
entries.handling: All three fixed in src/gems52/h57.py with a regression test for each the axis convention in particular, which had none.
entries.status: fixed; tests added

entries.title: The two-view co-training arm is refuted by its own pre-registered test (credited-core alternate round)
entries.status: open / disclosed
entries.what_it_is: H57-2 proposed a Blum & Mitchell two-view co-training emission. Its frozen validation (independence Spearman < 0.6 to proceed) returned Spearman 0.637 / Pearson 0.706 on 33 spatial blocks, and the joint model's top-5000 catalogue density (0.0236) did not beat the View-B single view (0.0244). The arm is ABANDONED as a scored candidate.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_validate.json (scripts/build_h57_cotrain.py --stage validate, exit 0); density and independence blocks recorded there; scripts/build_h57_emit.py carries the same disclosure in every artifact it writes.
entries.disposition: Not promoted. `--stage cotrain` / `--stage build` were deliberately never run. work/cache/gridscore_joint.npy is reused ONLY as ranker material for the H57 novel arm; the shipped metric bracket credits it with no validated gain, and the site/README/LATEST.txt state the refutation next to the download button.

entries.title: The prior family's per-cell credit allocation is under-determined; only an interval is knowable (credited-core alternate round)
entries.status: open / quantified
entries.what_it_is: Thirteen owner-reported scores plus the |G| = 14,088.7 px anchor identify the family's total credit but not its per-cell allocation: 574 coverage patterns vs 13 equations. A linear program gives the honest interval for the 25,517-cell credited core: [4,079.1, 5,249.2] px of credit (0.5 % slack on the 4-decimal reported scores). Adding 'more detectors agreeing implies not-less credit' makes the system INFEASIBLE — the reported scores contradict that monotone-consensus model.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/gems57_credit_lp2.json, evidence/gems57_credit_robust.json, work/credit_lp.py (the coarser coverage-count model is also infeasible, same reason); scipy HiGHS linprog.
entries.disposition: Every projection in the README/site/knowledge is published as a bracket (0.227-0.336 for the shipped file), not as a point forecast. The pair identity T(ref) = T(d2-8) = 5,223.13 is still exact and is what pins the anchor.

entries.title: The round-1 private truth is NOT the public labels — both public proxies mis-rank the family (credited-core alternate round)

Both orderings are contradicted by the actual report. Likewise the uncatalogued-SGMC proxy has no rank correlation with the reported scores (Spearman 0.193, p = 0.53).
entries.how_we_know: work/emit_decision.py -> evidence/gems57_emit_decision.json (exact metric on candidate layouts); evidence/gems57_instrument_validation.json (13 paired proxy/score rows).
entries.disposition: Neither public proxy may select or rank a candidate. Selection this session therefore rested on (a) the reported-score inversion, (b) the containment lattice, and (c) the frozen two-view gates — with the residual uncertainty published as a bracket.

entries.title: Tracked core rasters differ materially from manifest-pinned owner mirrors; the sample copy also contradicts the official description
entries.what_it_is: The tracked training, label, and sample rasters differ materially from the manifest-pinned owner-mirror copies in decoded pixel content, while their grid profiles match. The staged sample has ones on the staged labels, contrary to the official page's 'total fault absence' description.
entries.observation: The 23-file staged owner mirror passes manifest byte/hash verification, but the three tracked core rasters fail those pins and differ by decoded pixels despite identical grid metadata. training_features.tif has 97,207,447/233,304,040 decoded value mismatches (97,120,016 where both are valid; 87,431 validity-mask mismatches). labels.tif differs at 120,650 pixels despite equal class counts; positive masks intersect at only 663 pixels. sample_submission.tif differs at 60,988 cells: the staged mirror has ones exactly on the staged labels, contrary to the official page description of a sample predicting total fault absence.
entries.how_we_know: Streaming Rasterio pixelwise comparison of data/{training_features,labels,sample_submission}.tif and work/h58_pinned copies; byte/SHA and decoded mismatch counts are recorded in evidence/h58_preflight_integrity.json. The staging restore receipt records all 23 manifest pins passing.
entries.handling: Do not overwrite tracked TIFFs. The H58 runner read the separate work/h58_pinned data root and recorded hashes. The sample was used only for grid profile/finite domain, never for its pixel values. H58 refit View A, View B, and the union on the same staged bytes and folds; it did not reuse the old H57 result, whose input-hash linkage is absent. The H58 promotion gate still failed on severe support shortfall (IR-H58-002). Owner-mirror pin integrity is not organizer authentication.
entries.unverifiable: Which of the two pixel-level raster versions is the organizer-authentic competition input cannot be established from the staged GitHub mirror or the current tracked files. The raw official competition download is login-walled; the sample semantic conflict also remains unresolved.
entries.status: open - critical provenance issue; blocks any upload approval
entries.disposition: Use the staged files only for a clearly labelled owner-mirror research run. No weekly slot is authorized until organizer provenance/label alignment is resolved, even if a local holdout result is positive. Previous H57 scores are historical and not a pinned-data baseline until rerun.

entries.what_it_is: The frozen H58-A emitter produced only 22 of 37,654 requested nodes despite 123,173 positive F_geo support cells, so its primary holdout folds are not budget-comparable.
entries.title: The registered H58-A emitter produced a severe F_geo support shortfall
entries.observation: The frozen field has 123,173 positive-support pixels, but the output contains only 22 of the requested 37,654 cells (shortfall 37,632). Every primary hide and block fold is budget-incomparable; the local gate is false. The recorded negative mean lifts are not comparable-budget estimates and must not be treated as evidence against the geological hypothesis.
entries.how_we_know: evidence/h58_result.json and evidence/h58_holdout.json; the exact run source is bound by the code hashes in the result and was committed at b475f46. src/gems52/h57.py applies a 5-pixel square local-maximum filter before the 3-pixel Euclidean greedy exclusion. On the smooth radial F_geo field this leaves essentially site peaks, explaining the sparse output.
entries.handling: No zero-score backfill, threshold change, or post-result rerun was made. The TIFF is retained as a decoded-pattern-unique research artifact only; submission/LATEST.txt remains on H57 and no weekly slot was used. Any corrected emitter requires a fresh registration and a new complete run; it cannot replace this failed result.
entries.status: open — registered local gate failed on support capacity; no promotion
entries.disposition: Report the run as under-budget and non-comparable. Do not interpret its mean DTI deficit as a matched-budget refutation. Resolve by a separately preregistered, code-reviewed follow-up; do not alter the frozen H58 result.

entries.what_it_is: The pseudo-AUC proxy-negative mask used cross-connected raster dilation rather than the preregistered 500 m Euclidean catalogue clearance.
entries.title: Pseudo-AUC proxy-negative clearance did not implement a 500 m Euclidean exclusion
entries.observation: scripts/run_h58.py built the catalogue clearance with scipy.ndimage.binary_dilation(iterations=5) and its default cross-shaped connectivity. Pixels such as offset (3,3), about 424 m on this grid, remain eligible as proxy negatives despite being inside the preregistered 500 m Euclidean exclusion. The reported pseudo-AUC values therefore do not satisfy the frozen mask exactly.
entries.how_we_know: The run source bound in evidence/h58_result.json; compare the `cat_clearance` construction with `knowledge/19_hypotheses_H58_preregistered.md` and `registry/h58_preregistration.json`, which require at least 500 m from every catalogue pixel.
entries.handling: Treat pseudo-AUC numbers as exploratory and do not use them to support a co-training conclusion. The primary same-fold holdout gate does not use these AUC values and independently failed on budget comparability. No post-result mask edit or rerun was made.
entries.status: open — pseudo-AUC diagnostic mask is nonconforming
entries.disposition: Keep the raw values for audit with this limitation attached. A future diagnostic must use a Euclidean 500 m raster dilation and a newly frozen protocol; it cannot overwrite this run.

entries.title: The credited-core alternate was marked upload-approved without the registered comparable holdout
entries.what_it_is: The upstream H57 credited-core alternate receipt set approved_for_weekly_slot=true while its own slot_gate.not_measured says no held-out lift measurement exists. The standing no-slot rule requires a comparable matched-budget spatial holdout; the H58 preflight independently leaves organizer input provenance unresolved.
entries.how_we_know: docs/data/submission_h57_creditcore.json, scripts/publish_site_h57_creditcore.py, evidence/gems57_validate.json, README.md H57 acceptance sections, and IR-H58-001.
entries.handling: This branch supersedes that approval text: the H57 alternate remains downloadable as a research archive, approved_for_weekly_slot=false, and it does not replace submission/LATEST.txt. Do not upload or spend a weekly slot based on format, uniqueness, enrichment controls, or a metric bracket alone.
entries.status: open — research-only correction; no comparable holdout approval
entries.disposition: A registered comparable hide/block holdout and organizer-authenticated input/label provenance are absent for this alternate. Preserve its file/analysis but keep the slot gate closed.

entries.title: A second H59 build contaminated its own prior-scan and drifted the arm by 10 px
entries.what_it_is: build_h59_submission.py scans submission/ and docs/downloads/ for aligned priors; after the first build, its own outputs sat in those roots, so run 2 treated run 1's TIFF as prior support (47 -> 50 priors) and emitted a 14,777-px arm instead of 14,787 - the artifact was not a fixed point, which had been the claim made while proving determinism.
entries.how_we_know: Measured live in this session: same saved fields, same seed, different arm; the two stems differed (arm14787px vs arm14777px) while the receipts both said 'deterministic'.
entries.handling: prior_inventory() now excludes any path named gems52-h59* or h59-candidate*; the rebuild was re-run and verified byte-identical (sha256 e884f84a... both times, n_priors back to 47); a regression test (tests/test_h59.py::test_h59_prior_inventory_excludes_its_own_round) pins the self-exclusion.
entries.status: resolved - fixed in the build and covered by a test; the episode is itself the lesson: a prior scan must always exclude the round it is building
entries.disposition: Keep self-exclusion permanent; any future round copying this builder must inherit the filter or repeat the bug.

entries.title: Portal rejection 'Predicted values must be in range [0, 1]' reported by the owner
entries.what_it_is: The owner reported the DrivenData validator rejecting a submission with exactly that message. Every raster this repository ever served as a primary download that could produce it is one carrying non-finite pixels — every comparison against a NaN is False, so a single such pixel trips the range check, and the historical '-nan' alias exports (knowledge/09) plus a research-only NaN-bearing alias previously linked prominently on the site match the error exactly.
entries.how_we_know: Re-read of the served artifacts: the shipped H59/H57/H56 canonical files are all-finite {0,1} (verified from bytes); the demoted alias tif re-reads with NaN outside the footprint; the error string is what the portal returns for both non-finite and out-of-range values.
entries.handling: The site now leads with one-click all-finite artifacts (docs/executive-summary.html), the NaN-bearing alias is demoted and labelled, and gems52.grid.write_geotiff refuses to emit non-finite/out-of-range arrays at the source, with the build's format gate verifying the re-read bytes. If the owner re-submits the exact H59 bytes (sha256 e884f84a...) and STILL sees the range error, that would be new information: this file provably contains only 0.0 and 1.0, so the rejection would then point at transport corruption or the wrong file being uploaded, and the owner-side sha256 check in the ZIP's STATUS.txt is the first diagnostic.
entries.status: mitigated at source - open until an owner upload of the H59 bytes confirms it
entries.disposition: Never ship a primary download that re-reads non-finite; verify the uploaded file's sha256 equals the receipt's before reporting any portal rejection as unexplained.

entries.title: docs/submission/LATEST.txt had drifted to a two-rounds-old pointer
entries.what_it_is: The site-side pointer file still named a retired H53 artifact while the repository pointer (submission/LATEST.txt) named H57; a reader following the docs-tree link got a file whose receipt no longer matched docs/data/submission.json.
entries.how_we_know: Direct comparison during the H59 build; no test covered the docs-side copy.
entries.handling: docs/submission/LATEST.txt is now a copy of the root pointer (H57, since the slot gate keeps LATEST there); the H59 build updates both together when and only when approval flips.
entries.status: resolved - pointers mirrored
entries.disposition: If a future round automates docs/submission/, mirror rather than recompute.

entries.title: Two concurrent sessions both labelled a round 'H59'; the parallel one moved submission/LATEST.txt without a slot-gate receipt
entries.what_it_is: While this session's H59 co-training round was running (its preflight at 02:2x UTC), a parallel session merged PR #27 with its own H59 (multi-scale edge coherence + A-only boost, gems52-h59-edge-coh-cotrain-37654px-20261008T022050Z-0f0984928454.tif, sha256 4a60f941...) and repointed submission/LATEST.txt at it. Its receipt records format checks and novelty against h33 only (0.988 vs one prior) but no blocked holdout lift, no support-union gate over all priors, and no registered slot bar - the same approval-without-comparable-evidence pattern as IR-57-107. The collision also invalidated this session's determinism claim mid-flight: the prior-count grew from 47 to 49 rasters, so the fixed-point rebuild had to be redone honestly.
entries.how_we_know: git log on main (7c8c9d4 merge of PR #27, commit 9583756 dated 02:26:47Z); the parallel receipt evidence/gems52-h59-edge-coh-cotrain-37654px-20261008T022050Z-0f0984928454.json has no slot-gate fields; docs/data/submission.json on main still described the H57 pointer, so LATEST and the current-round receipt were decoupled by that move.
entries.handling: The merge of main into this branch (1) keeps every parallel-session artifact, page and receipt byte-intact (its TIFFs, h59-method.html, h59-evidence.html and its build script, now preserved verbatim as scripts/build_h59_edgecoh_submission.py); (2) reverts submission/LATEST.txt and docs/submission/LATEST.txt to the H57 pointer, because under the standing rule an artifact without a registered comparable holdout may not be the current pointer; (3) treats the parallel TIFF as a genuine prior: this session's build excluded only its own exact filenames (prefix exclusion would have wrongly hidden a real prior), re-ran against 49 rasters, and re-published (new canonical sha256 e87ee46c... - the honest consequence of a larger prior set, not a drift); (4) publishes disclosure paragraphs on index/executive-summary/downloads.
entries.status: reconciled - both rounds published; pointer discipline restored; future rounds must use unique round labels (adopt: date-prefixed ids) to prevent label collisions
entries.disposition: No upload or weekly slot is approved for EITHER H59 artifact; the parallel round remains downloadable research whose local numbers are format/uniqueness-only. The label collision itself is recorded so neither session's receipts can later be mistaken for the other's.

entries.title: A third concurrent 'H59' (view-B field) reached main moving the LATEST pointer and overwriting the short-path alias
entries.what_it_is: PR #30 (commit 867a2de) published gems52-h59-cotrain-view_B-37654px-20261008T033705Z-54debe0d-zeros.tif, rewrote docs/data/submission.json to describe it as the current round, pointed submission/LATEST.txt at it, and replaced docs/downloads/h59-candidate.zip with its own copy. The artifact itself checks out byte-honest (single-band float32, all finite, {0,1}, 37,654 px, EPSG:32611, 3730x3292 - re-verified during this merge), but its receipt carries no blocked-holdout lift, no all-prior support gate and no registered slot bar, and it reuses this session's scripts/run_h59.py path for a different 816-line program while borrowing this round's registration prose.
entries.how_we_know: git log origin/main (079f0b5 merge of PR #30; 867a2de file list) and the pre-merge submission.json/LATEST.txt contents on main; the run-script divergence measured as 484 insertions / 755 deletions against this session's runner.
entries.handling: Merge resolution on arena/3d4a53e2-gemsdoe52: (1) the view-B TIFF, ZIP, receipt and pages stay in the tree under their own names, and its runner is preserved verbatim as scripts/run_h59_viewb.py with a provenance note; (2) submission/LATEST.txt, docs/data/submission.json and the h59-candidate short paths are restored to this branch's state (H57 pointer; h59-candidate = the union artifact); (3) the pointer revert follows the same standing rule applied in IR-H59-004 and IR-57-107 - a format-valid artifact without a registered comparable holdout cannot be the current pointer; (4) the view-B TIFF is inside this round's 49-raster prior scan, so the canonical union artifact is novel against it by construction (the 03:49Z rebuild predates the merge by minutes - final hashes after this merge re-verified below by re-running the fixed-point build).
entries.status: reconciled - three concurrent rounds all published and labelled; pointer discipline restored; IR-H59-004's unique-label recommendation now has two confirmed collisions behind it
entries.disposition: The view-B round remains downloadable research; no upload or weekly slot approved without a registered holdout. If its owner record can produce one, the gate reopens identically to H59's.
